name: write-four-shorts-no-signed-byte-could-hold
rationale: An owned fixture whose only output is a texture2d<short, access::write>, writing the four shorts -32768, -129, 128 and 32767 -- every one of them outside the signed byte range, so a storage image only eight bits wide could not carry any of them and would leave 0, 127, -128 and -1 instead. It is the corpus's first signed 16-bit texture and its first authored air.write_texture_2d.s.v4i16. Note that it does NOT discriminate the storage-image format the emitter declares: MoltenVK writes through the bound texture's own format, so this case matches whether the module declares Rgba8i or Rgba16i. What it pins is that the signed-short write path binds, dispatches and round-trips every representable short.

name: manual-float4-fetch-depth-zero-triangle
rationale: Manual vertex fetch is explicitly enabled. Buffer 30 record zero points at three authored float4 positions and selects retained slot-zero float4 fetching; the remaining records are null. Identity object/projection transforms carry the fetched positions to the vertex observer, and the entry forces clip-space depth to exact zero.

name: linked-zero-work-half-convolution-weight-gradient
rationale: The selected static tile configuration keeps every derived divisor nonzero. All-zero gradient parameters give the sole invocation no output-channel or spatial work, so it reaches the kernel bounds exit before resource or linked-function writes and preserves the poisoned destination.

name: conv2d-a18-int32-int8-zero-shape
rationale: Zero convolution dimensions select no work while all exact postfix variants are linked.

name: linked-single-radix5-zero-write
rationale: One invocation selects one bounded radix-5 FFT work item. Unit extents and strides bound every destination-temp write to the authored output. The linked scalar prefix supplies exact one, the linked complex prefix supplies exact zero, and the linked postfix is inert.

name: mark-every-nonzero-signed-channel-of-a-two-by-two
rationale: Each of the four threads fetches its own signed texel, takes the componentwise absolute value and writes one where that magnitude is positive. The texels cover a negative value, an exact zero, INT_MAX and -INT_MAX, so the sign-magnitude conversion and the i1-to-i32 widening are both observed on every lane, and the all-zero texel proves the predicate is not vacuously true. Grid 2x2 writes every texel of the poisoned signed target exactly once.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-sixteen-rgb-lane-output
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 through 16 and receives exact float4 zero from all fifteen linked _uber_clear bodies. An eighteen-word size table and eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds; register 2 is selected. This entry splats the selected R, G, and B lanes into the complete poisoned 3x1 primary footprint byte-exactly.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-five-threadgroup-primary
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 through 5 and receives exact float4 zero from all four linked _uber_clear bodies. A seven-word size table and eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds; register 2 is selected. The single-invocation threadgroup executes both barriers over internal static storage and writes the linked result to the poisoned primary texel byte-exactly.

name: vertex-float2-position-expansion
rationale: Three authored float2 positions form a full-coverage triangle; the typed observer captures their structural expansion to clip-space float4 (x,y,0,1).

name: linked-single-uint-transpose-write
rationale: One dispatched invocation addresses one NDArray element. The reference-size and coordinate-mapping constants bound every dimension and stride to one; the linked prefix returns an exact nonzero value, the linked postfix writes it, and both callbacks are loop-free. Transpose variants use one initialized lane and the exact reflected dynamic threadgroup allocation.

name: constant-half4-red
rationale: The fragment entry ignores its position and float2 varying inputs and returns literal half4 (1,0,0,1) at color location zero; one full-coverage fragment must replace the complete poisoned pixel.

name: fused-depthwise-pointwise-zero-shape
rationale: Zero fused-convolution geometry bounds work while complete exact linkage is present.

name: vertex-float2-varying-passthrough
rationale: Three authored positions form a full-coverage triangle and constant float2 attributes traverse the declared varying; the typed observer captures its padded four-lane representation.

name: vertex-position-passthrough
rationale: Three authored float4 positions form a full-coverage triangle; the typed observer captures the passthrough position interface over the complete target.

name: resolve-a-bilinear-tap-from-a-gathered-array-footprint
rationale:
ksShadowOcclusionDownsampleSUDepthArray resolves one bilinear tap by hand: it gathers the four texels of the footprint with `air.gather_texture_2d_array.v4f16`, builds the four bilinear weights from the fractional part of the same coordinate, normalizes them by their own sum, and dots the two together -- once per array layer, walking the layer count the output texture reports. It reaches the coordinate through `air.convert.f.v2f16.u.v2i16` on the thread position assembled from `threadgroup_position_in_grid * threads_per_threadgroup + thread_position_in_threadgroup`.

The weights and the gather order have to agree, and this case is what says they do. The shader lays its four weights out as fy(1-fx), fx*fy, fx(1-fy), (1-fx)(1-fy); Metal's gather returns the footprint as (0,1), (1,1), (1,0), (0,0) from a base of floor(coord*extent - 0.5). Pairing them any other way would weight the wrong corner. The first and third weights are equal here, so the case cannot separate those two taps -- that is a property of the shader, not of the authoring -- but the second and fourth differ from them and from each other, so the diagonal pair is pinned.

Both textures are four by four so the coordinate maps one thread to one texel, and four is a power of two so the reciprocals the shader takes of the output extent are exact halves. The shader offsets by -0.498046875 rather than -0.5, and `fract` of an integer minus that is 0.501953125 whichever integer it is, negative or not -- so all sixteen threads share one weight vector, 257/512 and 255/512. Those are exact in binary32, their four products are exact, and the products sum to exactly one, so the normalizing divide is a divide by one and cannot round. Truncated to half the weights are 0.25, 0.251953125, 0.25 and 0.248046875 -- 128, 129, 128 and 127 over 512.

Every texel is an integer below four, so each dot product is (128a + 129b + 128c + 127d)/512 with a numerator below 2048: exact in binary16, and so is every partial sum, which is what makes the association the fast-math flags choose irrelevant. Twelve of the sixteen threads have a tap at column or row -1 and exercise the sampler's clamp to edge. The two layers carry different tables, so the loop over the output's array size has to advance the gather's layer operand with it.

This case holds no non-finite texel, so the four bit tests the shader runs on the gathered halves -- masking off the sign and comparing against the exponent-all-ones pattern -- all answer false and every tap reaches the dot product unchanged.

name: substitute-a-constant-for-a-gathered-quiet-nan
rationale:
ksShadowOcclusionDownsampleSUDepthArray resolves one bilinear tap by hand: it gathers the four texels of the footprint with `air.gather_texture_2d_array.v4f16`, builds the four bilinear weights from the fractional part of the same coordinate, normalizes them by their own sum, and dots the two together -- once per array layer, walking the layer count the output texture reports. This case makes one texel of layer 0 a quiet NaN, 0x7e00. Four threads gather that texel, each into a different lane of the footprint, so the substitution is observed once per lane and at three different weights. The test is an integer comparison on the bit pattern rather than a floating-point predicate, which is why the module's `no-nans-fp-math` does not make it dead.

name: qmm-n64-bfloat-zero-shape
rationale: Zero quantized multiply shape bounds work.

name: linked-zero-k-gather-qvm-n-bfloat
rationale: A single invocation and unit gather batch select literal index zero from the authored buffers. The quantized K extent and vector-row count are zero while the quantization group size is one, making every accumulation and final postfix loop zero-trip and leaving the sole bounded destination element unchanged.

name: splat-one-motion-vector-over-four-seeded-texels
rationale: A zero content scale keeps the splat footprint on the thread's own texel, so the single invocation issues all ten texture maxes at known coordinates and no two threads can race. The motion vector packs to the half bits of one and three, and a depth of exactly one supplies the high word, so the splatted word is known and the four seeded texels sit at, below, above and far above it -- the maxes therefore win twice, lose once, and leave the saturated texel alone. The thread's own texel also receives the second, unset-high-bit spelling of the same word, which is smaller, so it proves the operation is a maximum and not a store.

name: constant-buffer-float4-to-mrt2-highest
rationale: The loop-free fragment converts the exact finite float4 color in the 32-byte constant buffer to half4 and structurally inserts that same value into both return members; selecting attachment one verifies the complete two-target aggregate mapping.

name: zero-three-memset-lengths-that-do-not-match-their-object
rationale: Three llvm.memset calls whose LENGTH does not equal the object the destination pointer names, which is the whole difficulty of lowering memset without a byte address. Box is float2 + float + float. Clearing 4 of a Box's 16 bytes cuts through the float2, so emit_typed_zero_prefix (18 corpus sources, previously with no authored case) has to recurse into the vector and null only lane 0; clearing 12 bytes stores a whole null float2 and a null float and leaves f2 alone. The third clears sixteen bytes through a pointer to a SINGLE device float -- out + 8 -- which is the run the emitter used to answer with one store, silently leaving out[9..11] at their initial 0xAB pattern. Buffer 0 is (1, 2, 3, 4) so every surviving member is a distinct exact binary32 integer and every cleared one is zero: the answer is (0, 2, 3, 4, 0, 0, 0, 4, 0, 0, 0, 0). Clearing one lane too many writes 0 at slot 1; one too few writes 1 at slot 0 or 3 at slot 6; the short element run leaves 0xABABABAB in slots 9 through 11. The AIR is hand-written because the smallest corpus host for the over-long run is rwppRigidSolver at 908 lines, and no Metal source can spell a memset that outruns its pointee -- the frontend only produces one from an array element pointer, which is what the AIR does directly.
